quality_measured: Lower-limb explosive power / neuromuscular readiness proxy
test_name: Countermovement jump (CMJ) height
protocol_summary: 3 maximal CMJs, hands on hips or with arm swing (fix the variant and keep it constant), 30-60 s between reps; record best and mean. Standardise footwear, warm-up and time of day. Establish the athlete's own typical error over 3 baseline sessions before interpreting any change.
equipment_needed: Jump mat, force plate, or validated smartphone app; failing that, a wall-and-chalk vertical jump (lower precision)
age_band: 13+ (younger with coach judgement and light landing volume)
validity_evidence: Established as a measure of lower-limb explosive capability across sport; NOT validated as a boxing performance predictor. Boxing-specific evidence added 2026-08-08: in elite boxers a standardized prefight warm-up produced a 4.8% increase in CMJ height, and a 25-minute inactive gap between warm-up and boxing activity produced decreases in CMJ height and upper-body power (PMID 27191695). This establishes CMJ as sensitive to warm-up STATE in boxers; it still does NOT establish CMJ as a boxing performance predictor.
reliability_evidence: High relative reliability reported in elite athletes (ICC 0.97+ in the cited sample); PPBF must establish its own device-specific typical error
boxing_specific: Partly — general test, now with boxing-specific state-sensitivity data (PMID 27191695)
sensitivity_to_change: Moderate. In amateur boxers, CMJ height showed only a SMALL pre-post increase after boxing activity (SMD 0.33) — so it is a WEAK same-day fatigue marker in this sport
feasibility_in_gym: High (with a mat or app); Moderate (force plate)
safety_prerequisites: Cleared for landing/impact; no current lower-limb pain; adequate warm-up; suitable landing surface
youth_appropriateness: Appropriate from adolescence with low rep counts; avoid repeated maximal landings during rapid growth phases
normative_data_source: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — build local PPBF reference distribution
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (as a reliable power measure); INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE (as a boxing predictor)
retest_interval_guidance: Every 6-8 weeks for adaptation tracking. Do NOT use for daily readiness in boxing given the weak post-boxing signal.
human_authority_required: No — coach-administered. Any pain reported during testing routes to a qualified clinician.
citation_ref: PMID 40969919; PMID 35380916 (post-boxing CMJ response); PS extraction 2026-08-08

test_name: Isometric mid-thigh pull (IMTP)
protocol_summary: Standardised hip and knee angles, bar at mid-thigh, 2-3 maximal 3-5 s pulls with strong verbal encouragement, 2-3 min rest. Report PEAK VERTICAL FORCE only — time-dependent RFD derivatives are not sensitive enough to trend.
equipment_needed: Force plate and fixed bar/rack (portable force-plate systems validated in the cited studies)
validity_evidence: Well-established measure of maximal force production; correlates with jump and intermittent-fitness measures in young soccer players
reliability_evidence: Moderate to excellent within and between sessions (ICC 0.72-1.00 reported); BUT most parameters showed smallest worthwhile change LESS than the standard error of measurement — only peak force was 'usefully' sensitive
boxing_specific: No — general test
sensitivity_to_change: LOW for most derived parameters; acceptable for absolute and relative peak vertical force only
feasibility_in_gym: Low — requires a force plate PPBF may not have
safety_prerequisites: No current lumbar, hip or knee complaint; competent bracing technique taught first; progressive warm-up sets
youth_appropriateness: NOT recommended below 16; maximal isometric testing in growing athletes should be deferred in favour of qualitative strength competency
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (reliability); CONTESTED (sensitivity of derived parameters)
retest_interval_guidance: Every 8-12 weeks. Report peak force only.
human_authority_required: No — coach-administered; clinician referral on any pain

test_name: Seated or supine medicine ball throw
protocol_summary: Fixed seat/wall position, back in contact throughout, 3 maximal chest-pass throws with a fixed ball mass, 60 s rest; measure distance to first contact. Fix ball mass, seat position and release instruction across all retests.
equipment_needed: One medicine ball of fixed mass, tape measure, wall or fixed seat
validity_evidence: Validated as an upper-body power measure in older adults and in physically active male and female adults; NOT validated in boxers. Boxing-specific context added 2026-08-08: upper- and lower-body strength/power qualities correlate with punching impact in elite amateur boxers at r = 0.67-0.85 (PMID 26110348), and peak punch force relates to measured force qualities and body mass (PMID 32218063). Upper-body power tests are therefore relevant to punch impact as a CLASS; the medicine ball throw specifically remains unvalidated in boxers.
reliability_evidence: Acceptable reliability reported in the validation populations; PPBF must establish local typical error
boxing_specific: Partly — class-level boxing evidence (PMID 26110348, 32218063); this specific test unvalidated in boxers
sensitivity_to_change: Unknown in boxers — establish locally before trending
feasibility_in_gym: HIGH — near-zero cost, fits a nonprofit gym
safety_prerequisites: Shoulder cleared for overhead/press loading; no current shoulder or thoracic pain; clear throw zone
youth_appropriateness: Appropriate with an age-scaled ball mass and technique instruction
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (in non-boxing populations); transfer to boxing is an inference
retest_interval_guidance: Every 6-8 weeks
human_authority_required: No — coach-administered

test_name: Landmine punch throw (seated no-rotation, seated with rotation, standing whole-body)
protocol_summary: 3 maximal reps per variation per hand at a fixed load, 3 min between sets, peak velocity recorded. Test both dominant and non-dominant hand — the non-dominant hand was as reliable or more reliable in the source study.
equipment_needed: Landmine attachment or corner-braced barbell, plates, linear position transducer or velocity device
validity_evidence: Load-velocity relationships established in boxers; very strong linear group-average relationships reported. Boxing-specific transfer evidence added 2026-08-08: a short-term optimum power load program increased punching impact by ~8% with an effective transference coefficient of ~0.80 from jump-squat and half-squat performance to punch impact in elite boxers (PMID 31009434).
reliability_evidence: High INTRA-session reliability in boxers (ICC >0.91). BETWEEN-session reliability was NOT established — a genuine gap
boxing_specific: Yes — developed and tested in boxers; transfer to punch impact quantified (PMID 31009434)
sensitivity_to_change: Unknown between sessions — do not trend until PPBF establishes between-session error
feasibility_in_gym: Low — requires a velocity measurement device
safety_prerequisites: Shoulder and thoracic spine cleared; competent bracing; no current shoulder complaint
youth_appropriateness: Not recommended below 16 at maximal intent with external load
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (intra-session reliability in boxers)
retest_interval_guidance: TBD — cannot recommend an interval until between-session reliability is known
shadow_field_mapping: pilot.shadow_formula_observations (observation_kind='landmine_punch_peak_velocity_ms', context_id carries variation and hand)
human_authority_required: No — coach-administered

test_name: Countermovement push-up on force platforms
protocol_summary: 5 countermovement push-up repetitions on dual force platforms; derive peak force, mean force, flight time, rate of force development, impulse and vertical stiffness. Bilateral and unilateral variants.
equipment_needed: Dual force platforms
validity_evidence: Studied in elite Olympic boxers; the authors explicitly note NO gold-standard upper-limb force development test currently exists in boxing
reliability_evidence: Test-retest reliability examined across two sessions 7 days apart in 18 elite boxers
boxing_specific: Yes — conducted in elite boxers
sensitivity_to_change: Not established
feasibility_in_gym: Very low — dual force platforms are beyond most community gym budgets
safety_prerequisites: Shoulder, wrist and elbow cleared for loaded push-up; no current upper-limb complaint
youth_appropriateness: Not recommended for youth without individual assessment
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (reliability in an elite sample)
retest_interval_guidance: Every 8-12 weeks if equipment is available
human_authority_required: No — coach-administered

test_name: Instrumented punch force measurement (wall-mounted dynamometer or commercial punch-power device)
protocol_summary: Standardised stance distance and target height; fixed number of maximal punches per punch type (jab, cross, lead hook, rear hook) with full recovery between. MANDATORY: video the strikes to confirm perpendicular, centred contact — off-centre and inclined strikes reduced measured peak power by 15.9-41.4% on a commercial device.
equipment_needed: Wall-mounted load-cell dynamometer, instrumented bag, or commercial punch-power device; plus a camera
validity_evidence: Custom S-type load-cell dynamometers show good-to-excellent reliability and SEM below the smallest worthwhile change; commercial devices show large orientation-dependent error. Boxing-specific determinants added 2026-08-08: cross-punch force in highly trained amateur boxers relates to knee extensor peak torque and to ground reaction force and moment measures during execution (PMID 39074243); punching impact is higher in males than females and higher at self-selected than fixed distance for the jab (PMID 26110348). Distance condition and sex must be recorded or impact scores are not comparable.
reliability_evidence: Device-specific. Intra-session variability mostly small in experienced boxers; between-session variability moderate in untrained participants
boxing_specific: Yes — boxing-specific determinants and measurement conditions established
sensitivity_to_change: Good for a validated dynamometer with standardised orientation; POOR for an uncontrolled commercial device
feasibility_in_gym: Moderate — depends entirely on equipment access
safety_prerequisites: Hands correctly wrapped; gloves appropriate to the device; wrist and hand cleared; no current hand/wrist complaint (boxer's knuckle and CMC instability are the dominant elite boxing injuries)
youth_appropriateness: NOT appropriate for youth in the PPBF non-contact lane; maximal punching into a rigid target risks the hand/wrist
normative_data_available: No transferable normative data — values are device-specific and cannot be compared across devices
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (reliability under standardised conditions); INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE (norms)
retest_interval_guidance: Every 8-12 weeks, same device, same protocol, same orientation check
shadow_field_mapping: pilot.shadow_formula_observations (observation_kind='punch_peak_force_n'; device id and orientation-check status MUST be stored in source_reference_id and source_quality_notes; source_quality='low' if orientation unverified)
human_authority_required: No — coach-administered. Any hand/wrist pain routes immediately to a clinician.
citation_ref: PMID 42383407; PMID 36548503; PMID 29420389; PMID 28344531 (hand injury context); PS extraction 2026-08-08

quality_measured: Repeated punch output / sport-specific anaerobic capacity
test_name: 30-second maximal bag punch count
protocol_summary: 30 s of maximal-frequency punching on a heavy bag from a standardised distance, counted (manually or by video). Standardise punch type instruction, bag mass and stance distance.
equipment_needed: Heavy bag, timer, counter or video
age_band: 14+ with competent technique and wrapped hands
validity_evidence: In elite amateur boxers, 30-s bag punch count correlated ONLY with relative Wingate power and NOT with other anaerobic test indices — it measures something distinct and is not a substitute for other anaerobic tests
reliability_evidence: Not established in the located literature — PPBF must establish local reliability
boxing_specific: Yes — boxing-specific
sensitivity_to_change: Unknown — establish locally
feasibility_in_gym: VERY HIGH — a bag and a timer
safety_prerequisites: Hands wrapped, gloves worn, technique screened first; no current hand/wrist/shoulder complaint
youth_appropriateness: Appropriate for adolescents with sound technique and wrapped hands; not for the youngest Prep divisions at maximal intent
normative_data_source: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — build local reference distribution
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (that it measures a distinct quality); INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE (reliability, norms)
retest_interval_guidance: Every 4-6 weeks
human_authority_required: No — coach-administered

test_name: Upper-body (arm-crank) Wingate test
protocol_summary: 30 s all-out arm cranking against a body-mass-scaled resistance; record peak and mean power. Full standardised warm-up and a supervised cool-down are required.
equipment_needed: Arm ergometer with Wingate software
validity_evidence: Established anaerobic power test used in boxers; upper-body Wingate peak and mean power were the outcomes improved by boxing-specific repeated sprint training
reliability_evidence: Established in the general Wingate literature; not separately established in boxers by the located studies
boxing_specific: No — general test applied in boxers
sensitivity_to_change: Responsive: peak power improved 16.7% (d=1.10) after 4 weeks of sport-specific repeated sprint training in elite boxers
feasibility_in_gym: Low — requires an arm ergometer
safety_prerequisites: Screened for cardiovascular contraindications; maximal all-out effort — an exertion-tolerance screen and supervised recovery are required
youth_appropriateness: NOT recommended for youth — maximal all-out anaerobic testing in adolescents requires specific justification
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (as a sensitive outcome measure)
retest_interval_guidance: Every 8-12 weeks
human_authority_required: Pre-participation medical clearance on file before maximal exertion testing — clearance status surfaced by SHADOW, never determined by it

test_name: Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1
protocol_summary: Standard 20 m shuttle protocol with 10 s active recovery between shuttles, paced by audio track, to volitional exhaustion or two failures to reach the line.
equipment_needed: 20 m of flat space plus 5 m recovery zone, cones, audio track and speaker
age_band: 14+ (Level 1; consider a submaximal variant for younger)
validity_evidence: Validated: test-retest CV 4.9%; peak HR comparable to an incremental treadmill test; higher peak blood lactate; sensitive to training (elite soccer players improved 25 ± 6% versus 7% for VO2max)
reliability_evidence: Test-retest CV 4.9% in the original validation
boxing_specific: No — validated in soccer, NOT in boxing
sensitivity_to_change: HIGH — the test changed 25% where VO2max changed 7%, indicating strong sensitivity
feasibility_in_gym: HIGH — cones, tape and an audio track
safety_prerequisites: Cardiovascular screening on file; adequate footwear; non-slip surface; supervised cool-down; stop on symptoms
youth_appropriateness: Appropriate for adolescents with supervision and a clear stop-on-symptoms instruction
normative_data_available: Extensive normative data exist for team sports; NO boxing normative data
normative_data_source: Team-sport literature only — NOT transferable to boxing norms
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (validity and reliability in soccer); transfer to boxing is an inference
retest_interval_guidance: Every 6-8 weeks
human_authority_required: Pre-participation medical clearance on file before maximal field testing

quality_measured: Intermittent capacity with change of direction
test_name: 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test
protocol_summary: Incremental 40 m shuttle protocol with 30 s runs and 15 s passive recovery, audio-paced; record final running speed (VIFT).
equipment_needed: 40 m of flat space, cones, audio track and speaker
validity_evidence: Reliable, valid and useful across multiple populations including sub-elite female athletes and young elite ice hockey players (ICC >0.94; CV 1.6% for maximal speed)
reliability_evidence: ICC >0.94; CV 1.6% for maximal speed in the ice hockey validation
boxing_specific: No — validated outside boxing
sensitivity_to_change: Good — the final velocity metric has low measurement noise (CV 1.6%)
feasibility_in_gym: Moderate — needs 40 m of space
safety_prerequisites: Cardiovascular screening on file; adequate footwear; supervised cool-down; stop on symptoms
youth_appropriateness: Validated in young elite athletes; appropriate for adolescents with supervision
normative_data_available: Normative data exist for several team sports; NONE for boxing
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (validity and reliability outside boxing)
retest_interval_guidance: Every 6-8 weeks
human_authority_required: Pre-participation medical clearance on file before maximal field testing

test_name: Graded treadmill or cycle test to volitional exhaustion with gas analysis
protocol_summary: Progressive incremental protocol to exhaustion with expired gas analysis; VO2max, HRmax and where available ventilatory thresholds.
equipment_needed: Metabolic cart, treadmill or cycle ergometer, medical supervision
validity_evidence: Gold standard for aerobic capacity; used in boxing needs-analysis studies establishing that bout VO2 reaches ~89% of VO2max
reliability_evidence: Established in the general exercise-physiology literature
boxing_specific: No — general test used in boxing research
sensitivity_to_change: Moderate — VO2max changes slowly relative to intermittent field tests
feasibility_in_gym: NOT FEASIBLE at PPBF — refer to a partner laboratory if ever required
safety_prerequisites: Full pre-participation medical screening; physician-supervised where indicated
youth_appropriateness: Not recommended for routine youth testing
normative_data_available: Some boxing VO2max data exist in the literature but not as a usable normative table
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (as a criterion measure)
retest_interval_guidance: Annually at most, and only by referral
human_authority_required: Requires medical screening and qualified laboratory personnel; PPBF does not administer this

test_name: Handheld dynamometer isometric neck strength (flexion, extension, lateral flexion left/right)
protocol_summary: Seated with trunk stabilised; 3 s maximal isometric holds in each of four directions, 3 reps each, tester-braced handheld dynamometer at a standardised head landmark; record peak force and normalise to body mass.
equipment_needed: Handheld dynamometer (or a validated hand-held tension scale), fixed seat
validity_evidence: Neck strength CAN be reliably measured and CAN be increased by training. Its relationship to concussion risk is NOT established: a systematic review found no statistically significant strength differences across five planes of motion, another found zero studies reporting an injury-outcome effect, and a study in combat-training cadets found no effect of neck strength on head acceleration events
reliability_evidence: Handheld dynamometry shows acceptable inter-rater reliability where a standardised, braced position is used
boxing_specific: No — no boxing-specific validation located
sensitivity_to_change: Responsive to training (neck strength reliably increases); NOT established as a proxy for risk
feasibility_in_gym: High — a handheld dynamometer is affordable
safety_prerequisites: No current neck pain, radicular symptoms, or recent head/neck injury. ANY neck pain or neurological symptom is an immediate stop and clinician referral — never tested through.
youth_appropriateness: Not recommended below 16 without individual clinical input
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (measurability and trainability); INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE (protective effect)
retest_interval_guidance: Every 8-12 weeks if neck training is programmed
shadow_field_mapping: pilot.shadow_formula_observations (observation_kind='neck_isometric_peak_force_n', context_id=direction). MUST NOT feed any concussion-risk or clearance computation.
human_authority_required: No — coach-administered. Neck pain or neurological symptoms route immediately to a qualified clinician. SHADOW must NEVER link this value to head-injury risk output.

test_name: Handgrip dynamometry
protocol_summary: Standardised elbow angle (90 degrees, arm at side), 3 maximal 3-5 s squeezes per hand alternating, 30 s rest; record best per hand and the asymmetry.
equipment_needed: Handgrip dynamometer
validity_evidence: Handgrip strength was used as one of the profiling variables in a study of 227 young boxers (mean 15.65 y), alongside CMJ, punch velocity and rear-hand punch impact force
reliability_evidence: Handgrip dynamometry is widely used; PPBF must establish its own device-specific typical error
boxing_specific: No — general test used in a boxing profiling study
sensitivity_to_change: Unknown in boxers
feasibility_in_gym: VERY HIGH — a single inexpensive device
safety_prerequisites: No current hand, wrist or forearm pain; hand/wrist injuries are the dominant boxing training injury so ANY pain is a stop
youth_appropriateness: Appropriate for adolescents with an appropriately sized dynamometer
normative_data_available: General population norms exist; no boxing-specific norms located
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (feasible, widely used); INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE (boxing interpretation)
retest_interval_guidance: Every 6-8 weeks; also useful as a hand-health tracking variable alongside symptom reporting
human_authority_required: No — coach-administered. Hand/wrist pain routes to a clinician.

test_name: Punch velocity measurement (inertial sensor or high-frame-rate video)
protocol_summary: Fixed target distance and height; 3-5 maximal straight punches per hand with full recovery; record peak velocity. Fix stance, distance and target across retests.
equipment_needed: Inertial measurement unit or high-frame-rate camera with analysis software
validity_evidence: Punch velocity has been used as an outcome in boxing training studies including adolescent resistance-training comparisons and youth profiling
reliability_evidence: Not established in the located literature; device-dependent
boxing_specific: Yes — boxing-specific measure
sensitivity_to_change: Responsive to training in the located intervention studies
feasibility_in_gym: Moderate — depends on device access
safety_prerequisites: Hands wrapped; shoulder and elbow cleared; no current upper-limb complaint
youth_appropriateness: Appropriate for adolescents striking a bag or pads (not a rigid target) with sound technique
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (used as an outcome); INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE (reliability, norms)
retest_interval_guidance: Every 6-8 weeks
human_authority_required: No — coach-administered

quality_measured: Growth and maturation context (NOT a performance test)
test_name: Serial stature, sitting height and body mass; growth-rate tracking
protocol_summary: Standing stature and body mass measured at a consistent time of day by a trained staff member on a consistent schedule; sitting height only if maturity-offset estimation is used. Compute change in stature per unit time to identify rapid growth phases.
equipment_needed: Stadiometer, sitting-height box, calibrated scale
validity_evidence: Maturity offset equations show R2 0.92 (boys) and 0.91 (girls) with SEE ~0.5 y, but independent validation found they approximate observed age at peak height velocity only in AVERAGE maturers near PHV. Injury incidence and burden generally increase with maturity status and growth-related injuries peak during the adolescent growth spurt, with more rapid growth in stature associated with greater injury burden.
reliability_evidence: Anthropometry is reliable with trained measurers and a standard protocol; the maturity-offset PREDICTION carries substantial error for early and late maturers
boxing_specific: No — general youth-sport evidence; no boxing-specific data located
sensitivity_to_change: Growth rate is directly observable and meaningful; predicted maturity offset is not sensitive enough for individual decisions
feasibility_in_gym: High
staff_required: 1 trained staff member; measurement of minors under a documented protocol
safety_prerequisites: Guardian consent; measurement conducted respectfully in a non-private-exposure manner; NO pubertal staging, NO secondary sex characteristic assessment, NO skinfolds in the youth lane
youth_appropriateness: Designed for the youth lane; the constraint is safeguarding, not physiology
normative_data_available: General growth-reference data exist; no boxing-specific data
normative_data_source: General paediatric growth references (external); no boxing norms
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (growth-injury association); CONTESTED (individual maturity prediction accuracy)
retest_interval_guidance: Every 8-12 weeks during adolescence to detect rapid growth phases
shadow_field_mapping: pilot.athletes (dob), pilot.shadow_formula_observations (observation_kind='stature_cm','body_mass_kg','sitting_height_cm'); growth rate as a derived observation. Module 109 Growth/Maturation Context Layer.
human_authority_required: Guardian consent required; measurement of minors follows the PPBF safeguarding protocol. SHADOW may surface a rapid-growth CONTEXT FLAG for coach review; it must NOT auto-restrict participation.

quality_measured: Internal training load (primary PPBF monitoring metric)
test_name: Session RPE (sRPE) x session duration
protocol_summary: Athlete-reported RPE on a fixed scale (modified CR-10), collected at a CONSISTENT interval after every session (e.g. 20-30 min post), multiplied by session duration in minutes. Collect from the ATHLETE, not the coach.
equipment_needed: None — a phone or paper form
age_band: Adolescent and adult (use an age-appropriate scale and anchoring script for the youngest bands)
validity_evidence: 36 studies have examined the validity and reliability of the session-RPE method, confirming validity, good reliability and internal consistency across several sports; validated in karate and youth taekwondo; player sRPE was found to be a MORE valid tool than coaches' ratings; validated in adolescent athletes
reliability_evidence: Good reliability and internal consistency reported across the validation literature
boxing_specific: No — validated in other sports including combat sports; NO boxing-specific validation study was located
sensitivity_to_change: Good — subjective measures reflected acute and chronic training load with superior sensitivity and consistency to common objective measures in a systematic review of 56 studies
feasibility_in_gym: VERY HIGH — zero cost, fits a nonprofit $0-cost constraint
safety_prerequisites: None. Note: athletes may under-report to protect sparring or selection access — a reporting-integrity risk PPBF must manage culturally, not technically.
youth_appropriateness: Appropriate for adolescents with a standardised, age-appropriate scale and consistent anchoring instructions
normative_data_available: No boxing-specific normative load data located
normative_data_source: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — PPBF must build its own distribution
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE
retest_interval_guidance: Every session
shadow_field_mapping: pilot.sessions (rpe, date, athlete_id) — already EXISTS in the schema. Session duration must be added or derived.
human_authority_required: No — athlete self-report. Persistent high load with declining wellness is a COACH REVIEW trigger, never an automated restriction.

test_name: Brief daily or pre-session wellness questionnaire (sleep quality, sleep duration, fatigue, muscle soreness, mood, stress)
protocol_summary: Fixed short-item scale completed by the athlete before each session or daily. Interpret against the INDIVIDUAL's own rolling baseline, never against a squad or population threshold.
equipment_needed: None — a phone or paper form
validity_evidence: A systematic review of 56 studies found subjective and objective measures generally did not correlate and that subjective measures reflected acute and chronic training loads with superior sensitivity and consistency
reliability_evidence: Item-level reliability depends on the instrument; PPBF should fix one instrument and not change items mid-season
boxing_specific: No — general athlete evidence
sensitivity_to_change: Good relative to objective markers, per the cited systematic review
feasibility_in_gym: VERY HIGH — zero cost
safety_prerequisites: Reporting bias risk: athletes who want to spar may under-report symptoms. Any report of headache, dizziness, nausea, visual disturbance, confusion or 'not feeling right' after head contact is a CONCUSSION RECOGNITION trigger — remove from activity and route to a qualified medical professional immediately, per CRT6.
youth_appropriateness: Appropriate for adolescents; guardian visibility should follow the PPBF privacy tier policy
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE
retest_interval_guidance: Daily or pre-session
shadow_field_mapping: pilot.readiness (score, category, measured_at) — EXISTS. Item-level responses should be stored as separate observations rather than collapsed into a single score.
human_authority_required: Symptom items are RECOGNITION triggers routed to a qualified medical professional. SHADOW must NEVER compute a clearance, an all-clear, or a return-to-training decision from wellness data.

test_name: Counted sparring rounds, sparring intensity category, and coach-observed significant impacts
protocol_summary: For every sparring session log: number of rounds, round duration, intensity category (technical/light-contact/moderate/hard as defined in the PPBF sparring policy), partner, and a count of coach-observed significant head impacts. Aggregate to weekly and rolling 4-week sparring round counts per athlete.
equipment_needed: None — the existing PPBF sparring log
level_band: Amateur / Elite / any athlete who spars
age_band: Any athlete permitted to spar under the applicable governing-body rules
validity_evidence: PROXY, NOT A VALIDATED MEASURE. Justification: the number of sparring rounds completed by active professional fighters correlated with plasma neurofilament light (95% CI 0.0116-0.4053, p=0.0381), and weekly sparring rounds was the exposure variable in a regional brain volume analysis. Instrumented sensors are NOT a superior alternative in boxing: predefined quality criteria were met in only 53% (mouthguard), 20% (skin patch) and 26% (headgear patch) of 442 sparring events, with little to no agreement between sensors.
reliability_evidence: Round counting is highly reliable. Coach-observed impact counts are NOT reliable — human observers miss impacts and cannot judge magnitude. Intensity categories are ordinal coach judgements, not measurements.
boxing_specific: Yes — boxing-specific proxy
sensitivity_to_change: Cumulative round count is a countable exposure that changes with policy. Coach-observed impact counts have unknown and probably poor sensitivity.
feasibility_in_gym: VERY HIGH — this is the single highest-value zero-cost monitoring item PPBF can implement
safety_prerequisites: Sparring eligibility prerequisites must be satisfied first: registration, current medical clearance documented, no active medical suspension, qualified supervision present, minimum age met per the applicable governing body.
youth_appropriateness: PPBF's youth lane should be NON-CONTACT. The American Academy of Pediatrics and Canadian Paediatric Society oppose boxing as a sport for children and adolescents because it rewards deliberate blows to the head — PPBF must engage with this position rather than omit it.
normative_data_available: No validated exposure thresholds exist in any population
normative_data_source: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — there is NO validated safe sparring volume
evidence_class: STRONG EVIDENCE-SUPPORTED INFERENCE (round count is the right exposure variable); INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE (any threshold)
retest_interval_guidance: Continuous. Review cumulative exposure at every coach review.
shadow_field_mapping: EXISTS partially: pilot.video_sessions and the FLOOR_FLOWS sparring log emit START_ROUND/END_ROUND stamp events with durationSec and punch counts. ABSENT: an intensity_category field, a coach-observed-impact count, and a per-athlete cumulative sparring-round rollup. These are PROPOSED additions.
human_authority_required: MANDATORY. Cumulative exposure is surfaced to the coach and, where relevant, the guardian. SHADOW must NEVER compute a permitted sparring volume, a risk score, or a clearance. Any reduction or restriction is a coach and/or medical decision.

test_name: Concussion Recognition Tool 6 (CRT6) — coach-level recognition and immediate removal
protocol_summary: Any athlete with a suspected head injury or reported symptom is REMOVED from activity immediately and does not return that day. CRT6 is used by non-medical personnel to RECOGNISE and remove; it is not a diagnostic instrument. Referral to a qualified medical professional is mandatory.
equipment_needed: CRT6 card (free, published with the 6th consensus statement)
age_band: All ages (a child version of the assessment tools exists for clinicians)
validity_evidence: CRT6 was produced by the 6th International Conference on Concussion in Sport (Amsterdam 2022) informed by 10 systematic reviews. SCAT6, Child SCAT6, SCOAT6 and Child SCOAT6 are for appropriately trained clinicians, NOT coaches.
reliability_evidence: Recognition tools are screening aids; they do not have diagnostic accuracy sufficient to rule out concussion
boxing_specific: No — cross-sport consensus tool applicable to boxing
sensitivity_to_change: Not applicable — this is a recognition trigger, not a tracked metric
feasibility_in_gym: HIGH — free card, requires coach training
staff_required: Any trained coach can RECOGNISE and REMOVE; only a qualified medical professional can assess and clear
safety_prerequisites: IMMEDIATE REMOVAL on any suspected concussion. If any red flag is present (neck pain, deteriorating consciousness, repeated vomiting, seizure, weakness or tingling, severe or increasing headache, increasing agitation, visual disturbance) call emergency services.
youth_appropriateness: Fully applicable to youth. Youth concussion management is more conservative and is a clinician's determination.
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (consensus tool)
retest_interval_guidance: Not a scheduled test — used whenever a head injury is suspected
shadow_field_mapping: PROPOSED: a suspected_head_injury event writing to pilot.shadow_events and pilot.shadow_medical_administrative_status (status, restriction_flags, source_reference, set_by_role). pilot.shadow_medical_administrative_status ALREADY EXISTS and is the correct home. Module 078 Medical Uncertainty Routing Engine and Module 194 Red Flag Escalation Protocol.
human_authority_required: ABSOLUTE. Recognition and removal = coach. Assessment, diagnosis, management and return-to-training clearance = qualified medical personnel ONLY. SHADOW may record that a suspected injury event occurred, that a referral was made, and whether clearance documentation is on file. SHADOW must NEVER score a symptom checklist toward a clearance, compute a return date, or imply readiness.

quality_measured: Administrative medical clearance status (NOT a physical test)
test_name: Medical clearance documentation register
protocol_summary: Record, per athlete: clearance document type, issuing clinician, issue date, expiry date, restriction flags, and any active medical suspension with its source, start date and stated minimum duration. Surface status as: on file / missing / expired / suspension active / suspension minimum elapsed.
equipment_needed: None — a record field
validity_evidence: Governing bodies require documented medical clearance for participation and sparring. England Boxing requires an Annual Medical, a Fit to Box declaration and no active medical suspension before sparring. ABC regulatory guidelines set minimum medical suspensions of 30 days after a head-blow TKO and 60 days after a KO, a mandatory 7-day post-event rest, and state that the physician's decision to issue or extend a suspension is FINAL.
reliability_evidence: Not applicable — administrative record
boxing_specific: Yes — boxing/combat-sport regulatory requirement
sensitivity_to_change: Not applicable
feasibility_in_gym: VERY HIGH — the highest-value governance item in the battery
safety_prerequisites: This register is the gate that makes every other item in the battery safe to run.
youth_appropriateness: Fully applicable; guardian consent and youth documentation are additional requirements
evidence_class: VERIFIED EVIDENCE (regulatory requirement)
retest_interval_guidance: Check before every sparring session and every competition entry
shadow_field_mapping: EXISTS: pilot.medical_intake (clearance_status), pilot.shadow_medical_administrative_status (status, restriction_flags, source_reference, effective_at), pilot.waivers, pilot.documents. PARTIAL: an expiry date and a structured suspension record with minimum-duration and source fields are needed.
human_authority_required: ABSOLUTE BOUNDARY. SHADOW surfaces the administrative FACT (document present/absent/expired; suspension minimum elapsed yes/no) and flags missing documentation. SHADOW must NEVER convert an elapsed suspension minimum into a clearance, never infer fitness, and never permit participation. Only the qualified clinician who issued or can lift the suspension makes that decision.
citation_ref: ABC Regulatory Guidelines (abcboxing.com, fetched 2026-08-07); England Boxing Rule Book 2025 (englandboxing.org, fetched 2026-08-07); PMID 35678314 (Association of Ringside Physicians neuroimaging consensus)
